Overdue notices now say how late the item is. The body reads: `Hello Ada, "…" was due back on 2026-11-21. It is 5 days late. Please return it to any branch.` All 60 tests pass, including a new one for this.

- **Template:** in `lib/notices/templates.js` the overdue body gains `It is {lateBy} late.`
- **Days late:** `overdueNotices` in `lib/notices/digest.js` counts days from the due date to today. It uses `daysBetween`, the same calculation `assessLateFee` uses. A single day reads "1 day late", not "1 days late".
- **Test:** `test/notices.test.js` checks both "5 days late" and "1 day late".

The count is plain calendar days. It doesn't skip days the branch is closed, and it ignores the fee grace period.

The first run of the shell command that edited the files was blocked, so I made the changes with the edit tools. The first test run failed because I had assumed the wrong "today" in my new test (`TODAY` is 2026-11-26). I fixed the test's due dates, not the code.

I haven't committed anything.
